reconstructed_theorem_text: Let Ω be measurable with finite measure μ and let ℱ be a filtration indexed by ℝ₊=[0,∞). Let S be pseudometrizable with its Borel σ-algebra. Let X:ℝ₊×Ω→S be jointly measurable and strongly progressive, and let c:ℝ₊×S→ℝ be measurable. Fix any T∈ℝ₊ and p∈ℝ≥0∞ and assume one real C bounds |c(t,x)| for all t≤T and x∈S. Then b(t,ω)=c(t,X(t,ω)) is globally strongly progressive, meaning that for every cutoff a it is strongly measurable on [0,a]×Ω for the product of the induced time Borel structure and ℱ_a. Every sample section t↦b(t,ω) is integrable for λ_T, and (ω,t)↦b(t,ω) has MemLp exponent p for μ⊗λ_T. Here λ_T is real Lebesgue measure restricted to [0,T] and pulled back to ℝ₊ by NNReal.toReal.
objects: Measurable Ω, finite μ, filtration ℱ, pseudometrizable Borel S, X, measurable coefficient c, composed process b, horizon T, exponent p and bound C.
domains: X and b are time-first on ℝ₊×Ω, c is on ℝ₊×S. processFunction b(ω,t)=b(t,ω) is sample-first on Ω×ℝ₊. Its measure is μ.prod λ_T, with λ_T=Measure.comap NNReal.toReal (volume.restrict (Set.Icc 0 (↑T))). At each cutoff a, strong progressivity uses the time-first source Set.Iic(a)×Ω with the induced time measurable structure on Set.Iic(a)=[0,a] and the filtration σ-algebra ℱ_a on Ω.
quantifiers: All spaces, structures, X,c,T and p are arbitrary subject to the premises. One C bounds all times up to T and all states. The section assertion is for every ω, and strong progressivity quantifies at every time cutoff.
assumptions: Finite μ, pseudometrizable Borel S, joint measurability and strong progressivity of X, measurability of c, and the one-horizon uniform bound. No compactness, second countability or path continuity is stated.
conclusion: The conjunction consists of global strong progressivity of b, λ_T-integrability of every time section, and sample-first MemLp with arbitrary exponent p for μ⊗λ_T.
scopes: T=0 and the exponents p=0 and p=∞ are included. Integrability of time sections is pointwise over samples. The confirmed strong-progressivity product is time-first, with the measurable subtype [0,a] and ℱ_a at each cutoff a. The cutoff a ranges over all ℝ₊ independently of T. The separate MemLp product is sample-first and uses the ambient measure μ.
constant_dependencies: The bound C is uniform for the chosen T and all states. The conclusion supplies no quantitative norm estimate. The product time measure depends on T and its MemLp assertion on p, while progressivity is global.
